newsitem.title: JAPAN: Views divided as to whether dollar strong -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Views divided as to whether dollar strong -- EPA.

text.p: Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told a news conference on Tuesday that views are divided as to whether the dollar is strong at its current rate.
However, he added that there was no other currency than the U.S. dollar that could act as the key currency in the international market at the moment.
"Views are divided on whether the dollar is strong or not. However, in the absence of any other key currency the U.S. dollar's (position internationally) is strong," he said.
Asked about Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's comments overnight, Aso said that he did not think Japanese investors would shift their money to gold as it was not a familiar investment tool for them.
However, he said that with the financial reforms being carried out in Japan, financial institutions would in future be offering a variety of attractive products that might lure Japanese depositors.
Asked about the EPA's April index of leading indicators, which was below the so-called "boom-or-bust" mark of 50 for a fourth consecutive month, Aso said:
"Leading indicators tend to fluctuate, this time they may have fluctuated more than usual. I don't feel that the economy is slowing down."
He said it was difficult to predict how much the cooler-than-average weather forecast for the summer would affect the economy.
At the moment however, he said that the effect on consumer sentiment of other factors, such as the consumption tax increase on April 1, had not been as bad as expected.
